statement: Yemọja was originally a Yorùbá river deity, specifically associated with the Ògùn River in Nigeria (not to be confused with the Òrìṣà Ògún — same name root, different referent). In the Americas, her domain shifted from river to ocean, widely attested across Cuban Santería (as Yemayá) and Brazilian Candomblé (as Yemanjá); sources attribute this to enslaved communities "re-rooting" the deity in the body of water that carried them into bondage. The fact of this domain shift is well-attested across multiple converging sources; no specific named scholar's causal account of the mechanism was traced to one academic citation in this research pass.

sources.citation: Converging secondary sourcing on the Yemọja/Yemayá/Yemanjá river-to-ocean domain shift in the Americas.
